pattern.top_pattern: VA acute leukemia inpatient outlier in TANF Standard
pattern.what_is_impacting: VA / TANF Standard / ACUTE HOSPITAL / IP Med/Surg
pattern.pattern_details: A single inpatient acute leukemia case is driving the VA increase in TANF Standard acute hospital spend. The pattern is highly concentrated and looks like a rare catastrophic case rather than broad utilization growth. Because the clinical and operational views point to the same event, the right action is a case-level review of coding, medical necessity, and reimbursement together.
pattern.why_it_matters: One case is large enough to materially move results, so confirming its accuracy matters before any broader utilization or payment response.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Complete a case-level review of the VA acute leukemia admission covering diagnosis and procedure coding, level of care, and contract payment accuracy.
pattern.validation_reason: The increase is concentrated in a single low-baseline case with missing procedure detail, so the claim should be validated before broader action.
evidence_summary: One VA TANF Standard acute hospital case added about $1.9M.
Paid per admit increased by about $1.9M with 1 additional claim.
Acute Leukemia with MCC drove nearly all of the positive change in this slice.
Diagnosis C9201 appeared with no recorded procedure detail in the clinical view.
